Coupled-spin Lindblad dynamics

An interaction can correlate two spins before local damping acts on them. Treating each spin independently then misses the joint state and observables. This example advances the single-qubit Lindblad method to a coupled two-spin model, using exact local components and a symmetric global schedule.

Status

The two-spin gate/reset circuits are compared with an independently assembled Liouvillian exponential. Product and Bell inputs, local observables, ZZ and grouped energy readout are checked. A parameterized open-chain generator supports up to 16 systems; its larger circuit counts are executed separately from the bounded density study. A bounded local-observable study below covers n=2,3,4n=2,3,4n=2,3,4 with an exact-angle step policy and numerical reduced-state checks. The n2/r69 and n3/r134 physical slices are preserved. The separate literal n4/r211 trial has completed density/Clifford+T checks and an explicit controller-model rejection; its follow-on physical-wire-0 port has completed conditional reports for both frozen profiles. Full finite-angle certification, hardware validation and formal/Lean coverage remain planned.

Task and intuition¶

For two systems, set ℏ=1\hbar=1ℏ=1 and

H=0.6Z0Z1+0.35(X0+X1),Lj=γj∣0⟩j⟨1∣,H=0.6Z_0Z_1+0.35(X_0+X_1),\qquad L_j=\sqrt{\gamma_j}|0\rangle_j\langle1|,H=0.6Z0​Z1​+0.35(X0​+X1​),Lj​=γj​​∣0⟩j​⟨1∣,
(1)

with (γ0,γ1)=(0.8,0.5)(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)=(0.8,0.5)(γ0​,γ1​)=(0.8,0.5) and t=1t=1t=1. These are asymmetric model damping rates, not device-fault probabilities. Hamiltonian coefficients and rates are in inverse-time units. The initial product state has ∣+i⟩|+i\rangle∣+i⟩ on system0 and ∣+⟩|+\rangle∣+⟩ on system1; an explicitly prepared Bell state is also checked. Displayed system bitstrings read q1q0.

The target is the reduced density operator obeying the standard GKSL equation

ρ˙=−i[H,ρ]+∑j=01(LjρLj†−12{Lj†Lj,ρ}).\dot\rho=-i[H,\rho]+\sum_{j=0}^1\left(L_j\rho L_j^\dagger- \tfrac12\{L_j^\dagger L_j,\rho\}\right).ρ˙​=−i[H,ρ]+j=0∑1​(Lj​ρLj†​−21​{Lj†​Lj​,ρ}).
(2)

An observable task instead requests local X/Y/Z, ZZ, or the energy mean after this evolution. A retained state is defined before final system measurement. The exported circuits produce measured trials and ignore both environment outcomes.

GKSL theory supplies the model context Lindblad, 1976Gorini et al., 1976. Digital simulation alternates short channels whose individual construction is transparent. The symmetric sequence cancels the leading ordering bias while preserving positive substep times; the noncommuting components still produce a finite splitting error.

Actual components and global order¶

The ZZ component uses CX–RZ(2Js)R_Z(2Js)RZ​(2Js)–CX. The X layer uses RX(2hxs)R_X(2h_xs)RX​(2hx​s) on each system; its local X terms commute. Each damping component uses the survival-aware environment dilation, with a reset immediately before that environment’s next use. No dense Hamiltonian or channel matrix is a quantum gate.

For δ=t/r\delta=t/rδ=t/r, Lie order is chronological

ZZ(δ), X(δ), D0(δ), D1(δ).ZZ(\delta),\ X(\delta),\ D_0(\delta),\ D_1(\delta).ZZ(δ), X(δ), D0​(δ), D1​(δ).
(3)

The global second-order palindrome is

ZZ(δ/2), X(δ/2), D0(δ/2), D1(δ), D0(δ/2), X(δ/2), ZZ(δ/2).ZZ(\delta/2),\ X(\delta/2),\ D_0(\delta/2),\ D_1(\delta),\ D_0(\delta/2),\ X(\delta/2),\ ZZ(\delta/2).ZZ(δ/2), X(δ/2), D0​(δ/2), D1​(δ), D0​(δ/2), X(δ/2), ZZ(δ/2).
(4)

Every component receives total time δ\deltaδ. A half damping step has pj=1−e−γjδ/2p_j=1-e^{-\gamma_j\delta/2}pj​=1−e−γj​δ/2; it does not halve the full-step probability. Every substep is a valid positive-time channel. The two local damping channels commute, but this literal circuit still executes two D0D_0D0​ halves and one D1D_1D1​ full step.

ts.build_two_spin_circuit(time, J, hx, rates, steps=1, order=2, observable="Z").draw(output="mpl", fold=30)

System wires are q0/q1 and environments q2/q3. At rrr symmetric steps, environment0 is initialized 2r2r2r times and environment1 rrr times. Of these, 2r−12r-12r−1 and r−1r-1r−1 resets discard previous states before reuse. Known-input trials also reset both systems and include final measurements on all four wires. There is no environment postselection.

This is a global splitting over Hamiltonian terms and dissipators. It does not construct an exact combined-H substep with a separately added inner error. The full error already includes Hamiltonian-term and Hamiltonian/damping commutators. A damping-disabled H-only diagnostic is reported for interpretation and is not added again.

Lie–Trotter, Strang and Liouvillian product-formula literature provide context Trotter, 1959Strang, 1968Kliesch et al., 2011Kliesch et al., 2012. Their norm and dissipator conventions must match before importing constants; the numerical results below are not theorem or diamond-norm certificates.

Checked state and observables¶

The independent reference is a 16×1616\times1616×16 column-vectorized GKSL generator. It is assembled from time-scaled coefficients before exponentiation, avoiding large intermediate entries for short-time/large-coefficient inputs. Qiskit DensityMatrix evaluates the actual four-wire gates and resets, then traces q2/q3. The density reference is classical verification, not the quantum implementation Qiskit contributors, n.d.SciPy developers, n.d.Al-Mohy & Higham, 2009.

Another independent matrix calculation composes the stated exact component channels and checks that the circuit implements the advertised schedule. Tests cover product, Bell and small mixed inputs, trace, positivity, local X/Y/Z, ZZ and energy; removing required environment resets changes the channel. Mixed density matrices supplied to a checker initialize that classical simulator and do not implement arbitrary quantum input loading.

Analysis and verification: complete energy workload¶

X/Y/Z readout applies the appropriate basis change on each system, measures all wires, and ignores environment bits. Energy uses two incompatible measurement groups:

  • X group: one joint outcome gives score hx(x0+x1)∈[−0.7,0.7]h_x(x_0+x_1)\in[-0.7,0.7]hx​(x0​+x1​)∈[−0.7,0.7].

  • Z group: one joint outcome gives score Jz0z1∈[−0.6,0.6]Jz_0z_1\in[-0.6,0.6]Jz0​z1​∈[−0.6,0.6].

The bits within one trial can be correlated. Hoeffding applies to the complete bounded scalar score from each independent trial, without assuming independent spins. With statistical error 0.015 and failure probability 0.0025 per group, the proposal uses 29,116 X trials and 21,391 Z trials: 50,507 complete circuits. A union bound supplies total sampling error 0.03 and failure 0.005 for one fixed energy mean. Other local observables or settings need separate confidence allocations.

The logical ledger includes data preparation, all Hamiltonian/damping gates, every environment reset/discard, basis rotations and system/environment measurements for every group trial. It repeats the actual compiled counts across both shot allocations and records a logical qubit-layer volume. That volume is a dependency-layer proxy, not physical qubit-seconds: simulated time ttt and gate depth are not hardware elapsed time.

The proposed total energy-error target is 0.05, split into 0.01 global systematic bias, 0.01 coherent synthesis bias and 0.03 statistics. A coefficient bound ∥H∥≤∣J∣+2∣hx∣=1.3\|H\|\leq |J|+2|h_x|=1.3∥H∥≤∣J∣+2∣hx​∣=1.3 converts selected-state trace distance ddd to an energy-bias bound 2(1.3)d2(1.3)d2(1.3)d. The default r=32r=32r=32 check meets that systematic allowance numerically. It does not certify all inputs, parameters or larger systems.

Physical-fault probability is separately proposed at 0.005 across all 50,507 trials. Continuous-angle synthesis is pending for this energy task. Intended damping, splitting error, representation rounding, coherent approximation, statistical confidence and physical faults are distinct. The static physical adapter rejects mid-circuit resets; no complete physical estimate is supplied for this r32 energy workload.

Classical coefficient/angle preparation and readout processing, physical reset/discard/measurement time, routing, factories and code distance are excluded from the logical cost. Classical construction/decomposition and small density-check wall times are recorded as CPU measurements, not quantum performance. No quantum advantage is claimed for a classically tiny instance. Formal/Lean proof coverage is not integrated.

Size, accuracy and empirical scaling¶

For a general open chain, the executable generator uses H=J∑ZjZj+1+hx∑XjH=J\sum Z_jZ_{j+1}+h_x\sum X_jH=J∑Zj​Zj+1​+hx​∑Xj​ and one local damping environment per system. Its logical space is 2n2n2n wires. Before optimization, complete measured-source upper counts are

C1≤(10n−3)r+6n+8,C2≤(20n−12)r+6n+8.C_1\leq(10n-3)r+6n+8,\qquad C_2\leq(20n-12)r+6n+8.C1​≤(10n−3)r+6n+8,C2​≤(20n−12)r+6n+8.
(5)

The overhead includes preparation, system initialization, readout bases and all measurements; compiled operation counts are checked against an additional cap. Source calls therefore scale as O(nr)O(nr)O(nr) at fixed rrr. Actual construction/decomposition is run for n=1,2,3,4,8n=1,2,3,4,8n=1,2,3,4,8 and several step counts.

Local-observable workloads at preserved ideal accuracy¶

The bounded workload study materializes n=2,3,4n=2,3,4n=2,3,4 at a common output contract. It keeps J=0.6J=0.6J=0.6, hx=0.35h_x=0.35hx​=0.35, t=1t=1t=1, rate 0.8 at site 0 and rate 0.5 elsewhere, with ∣+i⟩|+i\rangle∣+i⟩ on system 0 and ∣+⟩|+\rangle∣+⟩ on the other systems. Each output is one final ⟨Z0⟩\langle Z_0\rangle⟨Z0​⟩, measured from a complete fresh-input trial; all other system and environment outcomes are ignored. This local-output task has a constant score range and a different measurement budget from the total energy task above.

The step count is chosen from an analytic bound before inspecting numerical errors. Use the trace norm on Hermitian matrices and its induced map norm. Hamiltonian commutators have norm at most 2∥H∥∞2\|H\|_\infty2∥H∥∞​ (operator norm), and a standard-GKSL local lowering dissipator has norm at most 2γj2\gamma_j2γj​. A component envelope is

An=2(n−1)∣J∣+2n∣hx∣+2∑jγj.A_n=2(n-1)|J|+2n|h_x|+2\sum_j\gamma_j.An​=2(n−1)∣J∣+2n∣hx​∣+2j∑​γj​.
(6)

Here F(s)F(s)F(s) is the literal reduced-system channel palindrome after environment discard, not the joint dilation unitary whose small-time angle has square-root behavior. Each component has total weight one, so F′(0)=G=∑cLcF'(0)=G=\sum_c\mathcal L_cF′(0)=G=∑c​Lc​; palindrome symmetry gives F′′(0)=G2F''(0)=G^2F′′(0)=G2. Every positive-time component exponential is CPTP and contractive. The product-rule multinomial expansion gives ∥F′′′(s)∥≤An3\|F'''(s)\|\leq A_n^3∥F′′′(s)∥≤An3​. The exact channel E(s)E(s)E(s) has the same third derivative bound, and palindrome symmetry makes their derivatives through order two agree at zero. Applying both integral Taylor remainders and then telescoping the rrr contractive steps yields

∥F(t/r)r(ρ)−etL(ρ)∥1≤Bn(r)=min⁡ ⁣(2,(Ant)33r2).\|F(t/r)^r(\rho)-e^{t\mathcal L}(\rho)\|_1 \leq B_n(r)=\min\!\left(2,\frac{(A_nt)^3}{3r^2}\right).∥F(t/r)r(ρ)−etL(ρ)∥1​≤Bn​(r)=min(2,3r2(An​t)3​).
(7)

This is a uniform exact-arithmetic, exact-substep evolution bound for all input density operators under the stated time-independent positive-time model. It excludes preparation faults, angle rounding, coherent synthesis and physical faults. It is a conservative original derivation for this schedule, not an imported Liouvillian commutator constant or a formal/Lean proof. The literature provides the surrounding method context Strang, 1968Kliesch et al., 2011Kliesch et al., 2012. A unit-norm local Pauli bias is bounded by BnB_nBn​, while state trace distance is bounded by Bn/2B_n/2Bn​/2.

Exact rational arithmetic selects the smallest rrr with Bn(r)≤0.01B_n(r)\leq0.01Bn​(r)≤0.01. Statistical error 0.03 per mean and family failure 0.005 are allocated across the three outputs: each case has failure 1/6001/6001/600 and 15,756 complete trials. Hoeffding’s threshold is checked with a positive exponential Taylor sum in exact rational arithmetic. In the ideal-angle model, a union bound gives all three means absolute error at most 0.04 each, with total sampling failure at most 0.005. The trial ensembles are calculated and unexecuted; finite-angle or hardware confidence is not certified.

The two-system report, three-system report and four-system report include the exact policy fractions, previous-integer failures, numerical checks and whole-trial ledgers. Counts include preparation, all literal damping halves, environment reuse/reset, basis/readout operations and every trial. Reset counts are 209, 673 and 1,481 per trial; all 4, 6 or 8 wires are measured. Lowering uses the pinned rotation/CX basis with optimization level 1 and seed 7; the table uses executed compiled counts, with compiler barriers recorded separately.

At the selected steps, the observed selected-input state trace-norm errors are approximately 3.59×10−53.59\times10^{-5}3.59×10−5, 1.39×10−51.39\times10^{-5}1.39×10−5 and 6.66×10−66.66\times10^{-6}6.66×10−6. These numerical values are separate from the uniform analytic bound. The exact reference is an independently assembled full GKSL exponential. The implemented reduced schedule is composed from matrix operators of the actual ZZ/RX and environment-dilation gates. Each environment can be traced after its dilation, because it is untouched until its next reset or ignored readout. Short whole 2n2n2n-wire density simulations check that causal contraction. The selected long workloads use powers of the gate-derived reduced channel, not whole-device gate-by-gate density simulation. Dense system states stop at 16×1616\times1616×16; channel/Liouvillian matrices at 256×256256\times256256×256; whole-circuit checks at four steps. No dense matrix is appended as a quantum operation.

For fixed coefficients the conservative envelope has An=O(n)A_n=O(n)An​=O(n), giving r=O(n3/2t3/2/ϵsplit)r=O(n^{3/2}t^{3/2}/\sqrt{\epsilon_{split}})r=O(n3/2t3/2/ϵsplit​​) and O(nr)O(nr)O(nr) logical work per trial. This gives a conditional algebraic workload scaling under the stated assumptions; the materialized evidence remains the three bounded sizes and is not optimal locality-aware complexity or a physical scaling result.

Scope of this logical family

The logical-family table supplies no physical qubits, code distance or hardware elapsed time. The single-spin conditional physical study covers its fixed two-wire task. The instrument backend defaults to five source wires and also has opt-in weighted-Kraus checks and QSP/thermal resource reports for other circuits. This logical wrapper itself supplies no coherent-synthesis or full physical report for its family. The following four-wire slice and explicit six-wire density slice have separate checks. This preserved wrapper has no eight-wire physical layer; the later literal n4 and port sections use separate opt-in domains. Extending the original wrapper requires actual synthesis/error budgets, wider reset-aware instrument checks, routed schedules and explicit data/factory geometry plus controller/reset/readout/idle-fault accounting. Changing a width constant would not validate those assumptions. The following physical slices are limited to the literal n2/r69 and n3/r134 tasks.

Offline coefficient/circuit construction and final statistical-processing wall time, Clifford+T synthesis, physical routing, factories, error correction and physical reset/readout/controller faults/times are excluded from the logical counts. CPU check times and logical qubit-layer proxies have separate labels. The frozen Grover baseline is unchanged; this is no matched co-design or advantage claim.

  • Source trials: 2 systems, 3 systems, 4 systems

  • Rotation/CX trials: 2 systems, 3 systems, 4 systems

Complete physical accounting for the literal two-spin workload¶

The bounded physical bundle fixes the local-output task above at n=2, r=69 and 15,756 complete trials. It keeps the +i/+ product input, J=0.6J=0.6J=0.6, hx=0.35h_x=0.35hx​=0.35, rates 0.8/0.5, t=1t=1t=1 and final Z0Z_0Z0​ score. Every trial retains both system initializations, all 138/69 environment initializations, each damping half and every readout. There are 209 resets and four measurements per trial, or 3,293,004 resets and 63,024 readouts in the calculated population. There is no algorithm postselection or retry saving. The trial ensemble and hardware schedule remain unexecuted.

The four-wire density path evaluates the literal source/reset circuit, rather than expanding reset histories into a pure-state ensemble. Setting the generic eight-wire limit would redirect even this small source into the branch-limited checker. The study instead declares max_qubits=4, 20,000 source instructions and 500,000 synthesized/validation instructions. The existing shared checker is unchanged.

The wider literal schedules retain the prior explicit ensemble rejection records. Their 6/8-wire sources fit instruction preflight limits, but the 256-branch ensemble rejects n3/r134 at step3 and n4/r211 at step2. The same ensemble rejects n2/r69 at step4; its separate four-wire density path is the supported route here. No nonzero branch is pruned, and short schedules that fit the ensemble do not replace the uniform-accuracy step choices. The new n3 density slice below supplies a separate supported route. In this preserved bundle, n4 synthesis and estimates remain unimplemented; the later literal n4 and port records use their own opt-in domains.

Protected Pauli-parity geometry, tracked Clifford frames, compatible factory/data handoff, memory and residual initialization models and independent majority-path readout remain conditional engineering assumptions Litinski, 2019Horsman et al., 2012. Offline coefficient/circuit/synthesis preprocessing and final statistical-reporting wall time are excluded from quantum runtime. Layout certification, decoder throughput and measured hardware calibration remain unavailable. This is a separate serialized scenario preserving the frozen Grover/PSSPC baseline; it is not a matched co-design or advantage claim.

The run is predeclared as one prepared circuit and two fixed physical profiles. Source diagnostics have a 60 s limit, the preparation/synthesis/check stage 600 s, each physical profile 180 s and the parent generation 1,200 s. Native rotation synthesis permits at most 3,312 attempts including retries. Each profile permits at most 24 top-level native factory and 24 top-level surface-code queries, with at most 1,000 factory candidates per query and 24,000 direct Trace estimates. Exceeding a cap rejects the complete stage; candidates are not silently truncated. Odd code distances stop at 49 and complete factory retries at 16. Managed JSON/QASM files stop at 32 MiB. These limits bound this small resource study rather than a wider-chain extrapolation.

Literal three-spin workload with full density checks¶

The three-system bundle extends the same local-output contract to n=3, r=134 and 15,756 complete trials. It keeps t=1t=1t=1, J=0.6J=0.6J=0.6, hx=0.35h_x=0.35hx​=0.35, rates 0.8/0.5/0.5 and the ∣+i⟩/∣+⟩/∣+⟩|+i\rangle/|+\rangle/|+\rangle∣+i⟩/∣+⟩/∣+⟩ input. The Hamiltonian is H=0.6(Z0Z1+Z1Z2)+0.35(X0+X1+X2)H=0.6(Z_0Z_1+Z_1Z_2)+0.35(X_0+X_1+X_2)H=0.6(Z0​Z1​+Z1​Z2​)+0.35(X0​+X1​+X2​). One trial gives one final Z0Z_0Z0​ score in {−1,+1}\{-1,+1\}{−1,+1}; the other system and environment readouts are ignored for that score. All three system outcomes remain correlated in the checker. The complete trial ensemble and hardware schedule are unexecuted.

The literal source has 4,435 instructions, including 673 resets and six readouts. System preparation resets all three system wires. Environments q3/q4/q5 are initialized 268/268/134 times; 267/267/133 of those resets discard their previous states before reuse. The calculated population therefore has 10,603,788 source resets and 94,536 readouts. There is no algorithm postselection, trajectory selection or shortened damping schedule.

The opt-in checker evolves the entire six-wire 64×6464\times6464×64 density operator. An unobserved reset on wire q applies the two Kraus terms

Rq(ρ)=∑b=01(∣0⟩⟨b∣)q ρ (∣b⟩⟨0∣)q.\mathcal R_q(\rho)=\sum_{b=0}^1 (|0\rangle\langle b|)_q\,\rho\,(|b\rangle\langle0|)_q.Rq​(ρ)=b=0∑1​(∣0⟩⟨b∣)q​ρ(∣b⟩⟨0∣)q​.
(8)

It sums both terms without recording a reset outcome. Ignored explicit readouts dephase their wire. No reset history becomes a measured bit, and no nonzero trajectory or physical operation is pruned. The checker may multiply consecutive one-qubit matrices to reduce classical verification work; the source and exported Clifford+T schedule still count every occurrence. The independent reference composes matrices from the actual local gates and environment dilations, and separately exponentiates the full GKSL generator Qiskit contributors, n.d.SciPy developers, n.d.Al-Mohy & Higham, 2009.

Literal three-spin Lindblad workload
def local_marginal(state,q):
    # Independent explicit partial trace in little-endian three-system order.
    result=np.zeros((2,2),dtype=complex)
    rest=[j for j in range(3) if j!=q]
    for a in range(2):
        for b in range(2):
            for x in range(4):
                offset=sum(((x>>k)&1)<<j for k,j in enumerate(rest))
                result[a,b]+=state[offset|(a<<q),offset|(b<<q)]
    return result
marginals=[local_marginal(rho,q) for q in range(3)]
product=np.kron(marginals[2],np.kron(marginals[1],marginals[0]))
assert abs(np.trace(observable@product).real-fresh["mean"])<guard
assert np.linalg.norm(rho-product,ord="nuc")>.7

    assert check["outcome_clbits"]==[0,1,2]

The new checker keeps defaults at five wires, 10,000 source instructions and 100,000 validation instructions. This fixed case explicitly opts into six wires, 20,000 source instructions and 1,000,000 routed/synthesized/validation instructions. Its hard density width is six. A retained complex128 density matrix occupies 64 KiB; this is a single-array size, not a measured process peak. The unitary-matrix cache has a 1 MiB default and 16 MiB hard ceiling. Instruction and definition caps also apply to generic unitary operations. The earlier ensemble backend and frozen n2 records are unchanged. The n4/r211 source is rejected by the six-wire width limit and by its separate 256-branch ensemble check; n4 synthesis and physical estimation remain unimplemented.

The complete source is lowered at optimization level 0 with full-unitary settings, fixed initial layout and SABRE seed 7 on the bidirectional six-wire line. The local lowering has 6,445 non-barrier operations and 1,358 event barriers, with 2,680 rotation occurrences: 1,340 RY, 804 RX and 536 RZ. Routing gives 5,524 neighboring CNOTs, including 2,442 routing additions, and 10,245 instructions including barriers. The initialized-wire schedule passes without extra resets. Every remaining rotation receives an actual ancilla-free Ross–Selinger sequence; repeated occurrences are charged even when the native synthesis target is cached Ross & Selinger, 2014Qiskit contributors, n.d.Qiskit community contributors, n.d.. The exported source, routed-rotation and Clifford+T QASM identify three different compilation stages. Measured-instrument QASM omits overall phase and is not a controlled-oracle specification. Coherent reuse of a unitary segment requires its phase convention and recorded in-memory phase.

The actual Clifford+T mean is 0.7910523096. Its system trace-norm discrepancy from the source is approximately 2.1483×10−62.1483\times10^{-6}2.1483×10−6, and its trace-norm error against GKSL is approximately 1.2711×10−51.2711\times10^{-5}1.2711×10−5. The complete emitted circuit has 707,581 instructions, including 1,358 barriers: 706,223 non-barrier primitives per trial, with 274,432 T gates and 5,524 neighboring CNOTs. The calculated population contains 11,127,249,588 primitive occurrences. Eight native synthesis calls produce eight unique rotation targets; the repeated sequences all remain in these counts.

The physical adapter retains the frozen p=10−3p=10^{-3}p=10−3 and 10-4 profiles and controller failure 10-15 per decision. It reserves 23 logical patches for data, workspace and bridges, plus one native factory. Each trial includes the six source-wire first resets and 17 additional workspace/bridge initializations. Startup, every reuse reset, every ignored readout, trial dispatch, active/idle exposure and actual neighboring CNOTs are charged. Each T/T-dagger carries complete capped factory retries, neighboring transport, injection/readout/corrective-frame work, port recycling and handoff residence. Output-quality and readiness budgets remain separate. The controller contribution is an additive engineering-model term, not a measured hardware-failure lower bound Microsoft, n.d.Litinski, 2019Horsman et al., 2012.

The 4,323,950,592 required magic states have a complete pipeline retry cap of seven, charging 30,267,654,144 capped pipeline attempts. Readiness is bounded separately by the modeled 1% pipeline-failure probability raised to that cap and union-bounded over all required states. Both profiles charge 692,984,803,680 controller decisions, giving contribution 0.00069298480368 within the unchanged 1/12001/12001/1200 physical allowance. The physical component sums also fit that allowance. Infeasibility and cap failures remain explicit in the adapter; no resource point establishes measured hardware confidence.

This run is bounded to one new prepared circuit and two fixed profiles. Source diagnostics have 60 s, preparation/synthesis/checking 1,200 s, each physical profile 180 s and the parent generation 1,800 s. Native rotation synthesis permits at most 10,720 attempts, including retries. Each profile permits 24 top-level native factory and 24 surface-code queries, with 1,000 factory candidates per query and 24,000 per profile; candidates are not silently truncated. Managed JSON/QASM stops at 32 MiB. The public artifact inventory records byte sizes, hashes and reuse of prior bundles. Offline coefficient/circuit/synthesis and final statistical-report wall time remain outside quantum runtime; layout certification, decoder throughput and measured hardware calibration remain unavailable. The frozen Grover/PSSPC baseline is preserved, and this small conditional study makes no advantage or matched co-design claim.

Literal four-spin workload in a separate bounded domain¶

This section follows the earlier n2/n3 bundles. Their negative n4 labels remain unchanged: the frozen six-wire density checker rejects eight wires, the 256-branch ensemble rejects the literal source, and the shared instrument materializer keeps its one-million-operation ceiling. The new n4 path uses separately named, mandatory opt-in APIs. It changes none of those defaults or historical rejection records.

The fixed task is n=4, r=211, local Z0 and 15,756 complete trials, with t=1t=1t=1, J=0.6J=0.6J=0.6, hx=0.35h_x=0.35hx​=0.35, rates 0.8/0.5/0.5/0.5 and ∣+i⟩/∣+⟩/∣+⟩/∣+⟩|+i\rangle/|+\rangle/|+\rangle/|+\rangle∣+i⟩/∣+⟩/∣+⟩/∣+⟩ input. Each trial reports one {−1,+1}\{-1,+1\}{−1,+1} score from the first system bit. It retains all four system outcomes, all four ignored environment readouts and every explicit reset. There is no quantum postselection or shortened schedule. The trial population and hardware schedule are unexecuted.

The literal source has 9,934 instructions, 1,481 resets and eight readouts. Four system wires are prepared once each. Environment resets occur 422/422/422/211 times, including 421/421/421/210 discards before reuse. Eight source first-wire initializations and 1,473 reuse resets remain distinct. The calculated population has 23,334,636 source resets and 126,048 explicit readouts. Frozen data/workspace/bridge geometry reserves 31 patches, adding 23 workspace startups per trial: 362,388 workspace startups and 488,436 startup preparations across the complete population.

Full correlated source verification¶

The new checker retains the entire eight-wire 256×256256\times256256×256 complex128 density operator: 1 MiB for that array. Reset sums both Kraus terms without recording a trajectory history; ignored readouts dephase. Before the first system readout it keeps the full 16×1616\times1616×16 four-system state and all 16 joint probabilities in logical c3c2c1c0 order. A product of single-system marginals is only a classical diagnostic: preserving Z0 does not preserve the selected interacting joint state.

Independent tensor/Kraus source preflight agrees with the gate-derived system state within approximately 7.73×10−147.73\times10^{-14}7.73×10−14 in trace norm. Its Z0 mean is approximately 0.7910514391, versus 0.7910507585 from a separately assembled GKSL exponential; the full-state trace-norm error against GKSL is approximately 6.66×10−66.66\times10^{-6}6.66×10−6 Qiskit contributors, n.d.SciPy developers, n.d.Al-Mohy & Higham, 2009. These selected-input numerical checks do not establish a uniform representation, compiler or hardware certificate.

def local_marginal(state,q):
    result=np.zeros((2,2),dtype=complex)
    rest=[j for j in range(4) if j!=q]
    for a in range(2):
        for b in range(2):
            for x in range(8):
                offset=sum(((x>>k)&1)<<j for k,j in enumerate(rest))
                result[a,b]+=state[offset|(a<<q),offset|(b<<q)]
    return result
marginals=[local_marginal(rho,q) for q in range(4)]
product=np.array([[1+0j]])
for q in reversed(range(4)):
    product=np.kron(product,marginals[q])
assert abs(np.trace(observable@product).real-fresh["mean"])<guard
assert np.linalg.norm(rho-product,ord="nuc")>.5
routed=science["routed_instrument_check"]
routed_rho=density(routed["reduced_before_output"])

For this selected source state, the product of four single-system marginals has the same Z0 mean but trace-norm discrepancy approximately 0.94795949. Adjacent ZZ witnesses are 0.43959675/0.42264155/0.43936007 in the source, versus 0.36753310/0.19578362/0.17071618 in that product. These selected-state diagnostics explain why agreement of one local mean is insufficient.

The explicit eight-wire API requires limits in its constructor and simulation call. The literal case opts into eight wires, 20,000 source instructions and 2,000,000 expanded validation operations; no existing width or default is raised. A 1 MiB matrix-cache budget has a 16 MiB hard ceiling. Ordered one/two-qubit index maps have a 128 KiB ceiling and larger maps are recomputed. The conservative 12 MiB dense-array workspace ledger excludes caches, Python objects, circuits and process overhead. Local matrix products reduce classical verification work without removing any quantum operation or modifying exports.

The state/trace guard is 10-8, fixed before observing the compiled result; full source/routed equivalence uses 10-10. The checker records raw trace and divides the captured reduced density by that trace once at output. With no acceptance labels this is numerical normalization, not algorithm postselection. Those guards are distinct from the unchanged error allowances and conditional norm premises. No formal interval or hardware-confidence certificate is supplied.

Actual source routing and bounded synthesis¶

Full-unitary optimization-level0 lowering keeps 5,908 rotations: RX1,688, RY2,954 and RZ1,266. It has 17,343 instructions including 2,978 event barriers. Fixed-layout SABRE seed7 on the bidirectional eight-wire line produces 24,510 routed rotation instructions and 14,130 neighboring CNOTs, including 7,167 routing additions. The initialized-wire checks pass without adding resets. The first-step drawing is exactly nine preparation instructions and the 47-instruction first literal period.

The separate compiler API has explicit 20,000-source, 100,000-routed and 2,000,000-emitted-Clifford+T bounds. It retains the frozen numerical Ross–Selinger policy, whole-trial allocation and phase convention Ross & Selinger, 2014Qiskit contributors, n.d.Qiskit community contributors, n.d.. A passing rotation-stage count is not a Clifford+T fit. An actual compiled trial must retain every reset/readout and pass the full correlated checks. A completed trial’s real operation count is also checked against the old one-million guard; this validation is not an executed legacy synthesis run.

Frozen physical model and explicit limits¶

The physical layer keeps p=10−3p=10^{-3}p=10−3 and 10-4, controller failure 10-15 per decision, and the earlier timing, geometry, memory, initialization, readout and factory-interface assumptions. It derives T/T-dagger wire positions and initial-reset classification from the actual emitted trial. The serialized model defines complete factory retries, startup, discard/reset, ignored readouts, dispatch, transport, injection/correction, recycling, handoff and active/idle exposure Microsoft, n.d.Litinski, 2019Horsman et al., 2012. An additive controller-model rejection is not a measured hardware-failure lower bound. Missing or unsupported physical points have no invented qubit count or runtime. If the controller-only diagnostic rejects its allocation, other fault components, factory searches and space/time remain unevaluated.

The next paragraphs retain the proposal at the original study’s completion. The separate completed port below implements its primary rewrite; the original rejection record remains intact.

The primary matched-task follow-on proposal adds an explicit eight-wire validation adapter, then amortizes movement over each verified rotation block. It moves the already initialized data wire to physical data wire0, nearest the unchanged factory interface, with adjacent SWAPs. It applies the same actual Clifford+T block using the existing T_q0 injection macro there, and reverses the SWAP chain before the next source event. Every rewritten block adds 6w6w6w neighboring CNOTs; none is free. The T_q0 macro retains its nonzero factory/workspace/handoff route costs. Blocks crossing uninitialized wires retain their original implementation. Actual sequences, phases, all 5,908 rotation occurrences, source events, error allocations and hardware geometry remain unchanged. A secondary bounded comparison may test eight predeclared cyclic initial layouts.

The eight individual blocks are not separate exports yet. The future bridge must extract them from the full Clifford+T export using the recorded rotation keys and segment lengths, then verify their phases, hashes and operators before reuse. No new native synthesis is needed only after those checks pass. Only a tiny full-unitary identity fixture supports the movement recipe; the complete n4 rewrite and native validation adapter are planned and unexecuted. The complete rewritten correlated instrument, added-CNOT/controller ledger, all repetitions and factory retries must be audited before both frozen physical/readiness sums are tested. A smaller controller count alone is insufficient. No physical feasibility or co-design gain is claimed.

ct_counts=None

first_resets=reuse_resets=0
if prepared is not None:
    text=(asset_dir/"clifford-t-trial.qasm").read_text()
    assert not re.search(r"^\s*gate\s",text,re.MULTILINE), "This pinned CT export must contain only explicit standard primitives."
    ct_counts=Counter()
    active=set()
    output_started=False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line=line.strip()
        measured=re.fullmatch(r"c\[(\d+)\]\s*=\s*measure\s+(?:q\[(\d+)\]|\$(\d+));",line)
        if measured:
            wire=int(measured.group(2) or measured.group(3))
            assert wire in active
            ct_counts["measure"]+=1
            output_started=True
            continue
        gate=re.match(r"^(h|x|y|z|s|sdg|t|tdg|cx|reset|barrier)\s+(.+);$",line)
        if not gate:
            continue
        name,arguments=gate.groups()
        wires=[int(q or physical) for q,physical in re.findall(r"q\[(\d+)\]|\$(\d+)",arguments)]
        ct_counts[name]+=1
        if name=="barrier":
            continue
        assert not output_started, "No quantum work may follow the first final readout."
        if name=="reset":
            assert len(wires)==1
            if wires[0] not in active:
                first_resets+=1
            else:
                reuse_resets+=1
            active.add(wires[0])
        else:
            assert set(wires)<=active
            if name=="cx":
                assert len(wires)==2 and abs(wires[0]-wires[1])==1
            if name in ("t","tdg"):
                assert len(wires)==1
                t_wires[(name,wires[0])]+=1
    assert dict(ct_counts)==synthesis["clifford_t_counts"]
    assert first_resets==8 and reuse_resets==1473 and ct_counts["measure"]==8

        decisions+=sum(number*(47+33*wire+4*retry+(name=="tdg")) for (name,wire),number in t_wires.items())
        assert decisions==diagnostic["controller_decisions_per_trial"]
        assert diagnostic["controller_decisions_all_trials"]==decisions*15756
        assert math.isclose(diagnostic["distance_independent_controller_model_contribution"],decisions*15756*1e-15,rel_tol=1e-14)
        table(pd.DataFrame([{"physical_error":report["profile"]["physical_error_rate"],"required_magic_states":states,"minimal_full_retry_cap":retry,"capped_pipeline_attempts":states*retry,"readiness_union_bound":float(states*Fraction(1,100)**retry),"controller_decisions_per_trial":decisions}]))
    if best:
        assert report["status"]=="computed_conditional_instrument_surface_code_model"
        for value in report["all_feasible_points"]:
            components=value["failure_components_all_attempts"]

            assert value["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"]==value["runtime_per_complete_attempt_ns"]*15756
            assert sum(row["count"]*row["time_ns"] for row in value["macro_ledger_per_complete_attempt"])==value["runtime_per_complete_attempt_ns"]
            assert supply["states_all_complete_attempts"]==states
            assert supply["worst_case_pipeline_attempts"]==states*supply["full_pipeline_retry_cap_per_state"]
        assert diagnostic["budget_exceeded"] is False
    if report["status"]=="infeasible_declared_controller_model":
        assert diagnostic["budget_exceeded"] is True
        assert diagnostic["distance_independent_controller_model_contribution"]>physical_budget
        assert decisions>52889904
        assert not report["pareto_points"] and not report["all_feasible_points"]
    rows.append({"physical_error":report["profile"]["physical_error_rate"],"status":report["status"],

Both unchanged profiles return infeasible_declared_controller_model. The actual ledger requires 123,409,809 controller decisions per trial, or 1,944,444,950,604 across all 15,756 trials. Its distance-independent additive model contribution is 0.001944444950604, exceeding the unchanged 1/1200≈0.00083333333333333331/1200\approx0.00083333333333333331/1200≈0.0008333333333333333 physical allowance. Code distance cannot remove this controller term in the declared model. No native factory or surface-code query was made, and no physical qubit count or runtime is reported.

The readiness arithmetic uses 10,119,826,704 required magic states, minimal full-pipeline retry cap 7, 70,838,786,928 capped pipeline attempts and bound 0.00010119826704. That is a separate modeled readiness union bound; native factory output quality and the remaining full physical components are unevaluated. The 52,889,904-decision maximum requires a reduction of at least 70,519,905 decisions per trial, a necessary but insufficient condition for the planned matched-task rewrite. The unchanged budgets, physical assumptions and historical negative n4 records remain.

The new run is bounded to one prepared task: source/legacy diagnostics 180 s, native preparation/checking 1,800 s, each physical child 180 s and a 2,400 s hard parent through export. Native synthesis permits at most 23,632 attempts, including retries. Each profile permits 24 top-level factory and 24 surface-code queries, at most 1,000 candidates per query and 24,000 per profile; overflow rejects the whole profile. Managed JSON/QASM has a 32 MiB cap and private checkpoints a 256 MiB cap. Cap, numerical-check or controller failures remain explicit; no stale success or partial trial is described as complete.

Offline coefficient/circuit/synthesis and reporting wall time is outside quantum runtime. Certified layout, decoder throughput and measured hardware calibration are unavailable. Full-family physical confidence, a feasible n4 hardware schedule and any matched co-design improvement remain unimplemented.

Physical-wire-0 port: a model-feasible follow-on¶

Long Clifford+T words offer a different place to pay for transport. In the frozen model, each T injection has wire-dependent transport and controller costs. The port moves the affected state to the factory’s data-wire-0 interface once for an entire word, executes that same word there, and restores the wire positions before the next source event. Here “wire 0” is a routed data-wire position; the encoded physical qubits are counted separately.

This is the same n=4, r=211, local Z0 task and all 15,756 complete trials, with the same input, Hamiltonian, damping rates, error allocations, physical profiles, bidirectional eight-wire line, 31 patches and factory interface as the literal record above. The repeated trial population and hardware schedule are unexecuted. The original implementation remains infeasible_declared_controller_model, with no evaluated physical qubits or runtime. The port supplies its own conditional model points.

Actual words and transport construction¶

The recovered catalogue contains eight actual native words, with lengths 462/233/225/225/230/230/244/244: 2,093 distinct-word primitives. All 5,908 occurrences match the saved complete stream. Their full phased operators, explicit QASM gphase and binary64 phase sidecars are retained; word recovery starts no new rotation synthesis Ross & Selinger, 2014Qiskit contributors, n.d.Qiskit community contributors, n.d..

For an eligible initialized wire www, let SwS_wSw​ be the descending adjacent SWAP chain that moves its state to wire 0. Let WwW_wWw​ be the bare token word. The chronological construction is that chain, the unchanged bare word on wire 0, then the reverse chain:

Ww⟼Sw†W0Sw.W_w\longmapsto S_w^\dagger W_0 S_w.Ww​⟼Sw†​W0​Sw​.
(9)

The swaps transport correlations as well as the local state. Each SWAP is three neighboring CX gates, so the outward and return paths charge 6w6w6w actual CX per word. The T_q0 macro still charges its nonzero factory, workspace, handoff, transport and injection costs. The recipe uses bare words plus the authoritative baseline whole phase exactly once. The complete candidate QASM retains one explicit overall gphase; the phase-bearing word exports are operator references and their phase must not be added again. All actual paths were eligible; the implementation keeps the original word for unsafe paths, with that fallback covered by tiny fixtures.

if source_ready:
    words = catalog["words"]
    assert catalog["word_count"] == len(words) == 8
    assert sum(word["operations"] for word in words) == 2093
    assert sum(word["occurrences"] for word in words) == 5908
    assert catalog["new_synthesis_calls"] == 0
    catalog_payload = dict(catalog)
    catalog_digest = catalog_payload.pop("recovery_sha256")
    assert hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes(catalog_payload)).hexdigest() == catalog_digest
    primitive_matrices = {
        "h": np.array([[1,1],[1,-1]], complex)/math.sqrt(2),
        "t": np.diag([1,np.exp(1j*math.pi/4)]),
        "tdg": np.diag([1,np.exp(-1j*math.pi/4)]),
        "s": np.diag([1,1j]), "sdg": np.diag([1,-1j]),
        "x": np.array([[0,1],[1,0]], complex),
        "y": np.array([[0,-1j],[1j,0]], complex), "z": np.diag([1,-1])}
    operator_residuals = []
    phase_omission_residuals = []
    for word in words:
        phase = float.fromhex(word["global_phase_binary64_hex"])
        assert word["global_phase_radians"] == phase
        assert word["operations"] == len(word["tokens"]) == sum(word["gate_counts"].values())
        assert hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes(word["tokens"])).hexdigest() == word["sequence_sha256"]
        raw = file_bytes(word["qasm_path"], 32*1024)
        assert hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() == word["qasm_sha256"]
        lines = raw.decode().splitlines()
        assert lines[:3] == ["OPENQASM 3.0;", 'include "stdgates.inc";', "qubit[1] q;"]
        assert lines[3] == f"gphase({phase!r});"
        assert lines[4:] == [f'{token["name"]} q[0];' for token in word["tokens"]]
        bare = np.eye(2, dtype=complex)
        counts = Counter()
        for token in word["tokens"]:
            assert token["qubits"] == [0] and token["clbits"] == token["params_hex"] == []
            bare = primitive_matrices[token["name"]] @ bare
            counts[token["name"]] += 1
        assert dict(counts) == word["gate_counts"]
        actual = np.exp(1j*phase)*bare
        recorded = np.array(word["matrix"]["real"]) + 1j*np.array(word["matrix"]["imag"])
        assert recorded.shape == (2,2) and np.isfinite(recorded).all()
        residual = float(np.linalg.norm(actual-recorded, "fro"))
        operator_residuals.append(residual)
        assert residual <= 1e-12
        angle = float.fromhex(word["angle_hex"])
        c,s = math.cos(angle/2), math.sin(angle/2)
        axis = word["rotation_gate"]
        assert axis in {"rx","ry","rz"}
        target = np.array([[c,-1j*s],[-1j*s,c]]) if axis == "rx" else np.array([[c,-s],[s,c]]) if axis == "ry" else np.diag([np.exp(-1j*angle/2),np.exp(1j*angle/2)])
        guarded_error = float(np.linalg.norm(actual-target, "fro")) + 1e-12
        assert abs(guarded_error-word["recorded_guarded_frobenius_error"]) <= 1e-12
        phase_omission_residuals.append(float(np.linalg.norm(bare-recorded,"fro")))
    table([{"word":w["word_id"], "rotation":w["rotation_gate"], "primitives":w["operations"], "occurrences":w["occurrences"], "T":w["gate_counts"].get("t",0)+w["gate_counts"].get("tdg",0), "recorded guarded error":w["recorded_guarded_frobenius_error"]} for w in words])
    print("Maximum full phased-operator replay residual:", max(operator_residuals))
    print("Phase-omitted residual range:", min(phase_omission_residuals), max(phase_omission_residuals))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8,3.2))
    x = np.arange(len(words))
    bottom = np.zeros(len(words))
    for gate,color in (("h","#477da8"),("t","#c18544"),("s","#7b8e6a"),("x","#967bab")):
        heights=np.array([w["gate_counts"].get(gate,0) for w in words])
        ax.bar(x, heights, bottom=bottom, label=gate.upper(), color=color)
        bottom += heights
    ax.set_xticks(x, [w["word_id"] for w in words], rotation=25, ha="right")
    ax.set_ylabel("Actual primitives per distinct word")
    ax.set_title("Eight saved native words; phases are recorded separately")
    ax.legend(ncol=4, frameon=False)
    ax.spines[["top","right"]].set_visible(False)
    fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
else:
    print("Recovered-word table pending source-stage export.")

Complete conditional surface-code accounting¶

The port requires 50,713,680 controller decisions per trial and 799,044,742,080 across the calculated population. Its controller-model contribution 0.00079904474208 meets the unchanged 1/12001/12001/1200 share; the original 123,409,809 decisions per trial still fails that share. This controller calculation is an eligibility check. The complete physical reports additionally charge all source operations, added CX, startup, resets/readouts, dispatch, transport/injection, full factory retries, storage and active/idle exposure Microsoft, n.d.Litinski, 2019Horsman et al., 2012.

profiles = results.get("physical_profiles", []) if results else []
if not profiles:
    print("No completed native profile record is available. No physical feasibility or co-design gain is claimed.")
else:
    assert len(profiles) == 2
    def macro_cost(name, profile, distance, factory_ns, cap):
        dtime = distance*profile["code_cycle_time_ns"]
        init = profile["physical_initialization_time_ns"]+dtime+profile["reaction_time_ns"]
        destructive = profile["physical_measurement_time_ns"]+profile["reaction_time_ns"]
        parity = 2*init+dtime+destructive
        cnot = 3*parity+2*profile["reaction_time_ns"]
        if name == "initial_reset": return (init,0,1,1)
        if name == "reset": return (parity+2*profile["reaction_time_ns"]+dtime,1,2,5)
        if name == "measure": return (parity,1,2,3)
        if name == "cx": return (cnot,3,6,11)
        if name.startswith(("t_q","tdg_q")):
            wire=int(name.split("_q")[1]); cnots=3*(wire+1)+1
            inverse=int(name.startswith("tdg"))
            overhead=profile["physical_initialization_time_ns"]+profile["physical_measurement_time_ns"]+profile["reaction_time_ns"]
            supply=cap*(factory_ns+profile["factory_feedback_rounds_reserved"]*overhead+profile["reaction_time_ns"])
            return (supply+cnots*cnot+destructive+profile["reaction_time_ns"]+init+inverse*profile["reaction_time_ns"],3*cnots+1,6*cnots+1,11*cnots+3+inverse+cap*(profile["factory_feedback_rounds_reserved"]+1))
        assert name in {"h","s","sdg","x","y","z","trial_control"}, name
        return (profile["reaction_time_ns"],0,0,1)
    def close(actual, expected):
        assert math.isclose(actual,expected,rel_tol=1e-10,abs_tol=1e-18),(actual,expected)
    physical_float=float(Fraction(1,1200))
    if Fraction.from_float(physical_float) > Fraction(1,1200):
        physical_float=math.nextafter(physical_float,-math.inf)
    summaries=[]; frontier_rows=[]
    for index, report in enumerate(profiles):
        expected_rate=(1e-3,1e-4)[index]
        profile=report.get("profile")
        if profile is not None:
            assert profile["physical_error_rate"] == expected_rate
            assert profile["controller_failure_per_decision"] == 1e-15
            assert profile["maximum_code_distance"] == 49 and profile["factory_feedback_rounds_reserved"] == 3
            assert profile["factory_pipeline_failure_bound"] == .01
        if "physical_failure_budget" in report or "factory_availability_budget" in report:
            assert report["physical_failure_budget"] == report["factory_availability_budget"] == physical_float
        ledger=report.get("native_execution",{})
        for name,cap in (("factory_queries",24),("surface_code_queries",24),("factory_candidates_observed_within_cap",24000)):
            if name in ledger: assert 0 <= ledger[name] <= cap, name
        if "factory_candidates_observed_within_cap" in ledger:
            assert 0 <= ledger["trace_estimates"] <= ledger["factory_candidates_observed_within_cap"]
        points=report.get("pareto_points",[])
        all_points=report.get("all_feasible_points",[])
        assert len(points) <= len(all_points) <= 24000
        if report["status"] == "computed_conditional_port_surface_code_model":
            assert points and all_points and len(all_points) == report["feasible_candidate_count"]
            assert report["physical_failure_budget"] == report["factory_availability_budget"] == physical_float
            assert report["complete_algorithm_attempts"] == 15756
            assert report["workspace_initializations_per_attempt"] == 23
            assert report["synthesized_event_counts"] == candidate["candidate_report"]["gate_counts"]
            assert report["verification_fingerprint"] == results["candidate_verification_fingerprint"]
            expected_events={k:v for k,v in candidate["candidate_report"]["gate_counts"].items() if k not in {"barrier","t","tdg","reset"}}
            expected_events.update({"initial_reset":31,"reset":1473,"trial_control":1,"t_q0":642284})
            for point in all_points:
                distance=point["data_code_distance"]
                assert distance in range(3,50,2) and point["reserved_logical_patches"] == 31
                assert point["data_workspace_physical_qubits"] == 31*(2*distance**2-1)
                assert point["peak_physical_qubits"] == point["data_workspace_physical_qubits"]+point["factory_physical_qubits"]
                factory=point["factory_supply"]
                assert factory["states_all_complete_attempts"] == magic_states
                assert factory["full_pipeline_retry_cap_per_state"] == retry_cap
                assert factory["worst_case_pipeline_attempts"] == magic_states*retry_cap
                close(factory["availability_failure_union_bound"],readiness_bound)
                assert factory["availability_failure_union_bound"] <= report["factory_availability_budget"]
                rows=point["macro_ledger_per_complete_attempt"]
                assert {r["operation"]:r["count"] for r in rows} == expected_events
                for row in rows:
                    expected=macro_cost(row["operation"],profile,distance,factory["pipeline_time_ns"],retry_cap)
                    assert tuple(row[key] for key in ("time_ns","readouts","preparations","decisions")) == expected
                runtime=sum(r["count"]*r["time_ns"] for r in rows)
                assert runtime == point["runtime_per_complete_attempt_ns"]
                assert runtime*15756 == point["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"]
                assert sum(r["count"]*r["decisions"] for r in rows) == controller_per_trial
                components=point["failure_components_all_attempts"]
                close(components["controller_scenario"],controller_contribution)
                close(components["factory_output_quality_model"],magic_states*factory["output_error"])
                close(sum(components.values()),point["full_physical_failure_model"])
                assert point["full_physical_failure_model"] <= report["physical_failure_budget"]
            # Sorted distinct pairs provide an O(N log N) nondominance replay.
            nondominated=set(); best_runtime=math.inf
            pairs=sorted({(p["peak_physical_qubits"],p["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"]) for p in all_points})
            for qubits,runtime in pairs:
                if runtime < best_runtime:
                    nondominated.add((qubits,runtime)); best_runtime=runtime
            assert {(p["peak_physical_qubits"],p["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"]) for p in points} == nondominated
            frontier_rows.extend({"p":expected_rate,"distance":point["data_code_distance"],"physical qubits":point["peak_physical_qubits"],"calculated population runtime (s)":point["worst_case_runtime_all_attempts_ns"]/1e9,"physical failure sum":point["full_physical_failure_model"],"readiness bound":point["factory_supply"]["availability_failure_union_bound"]} for point in points)
        else:
            assert not points
            assert not all_points
        summaries.append({"p":expected_rate,"status":report["status"],"Pareto points":len(points),"factory queries":ledger.get("factory_queries"),"surface-code queries":ledger.get("surface_code_queries"),"returned candidates within cap":ledger.get("factory_candidates_observed_within_cap"),"Trace estimates":ledger.get("trace_estimates"),"reason":report.get("reason","")})
    table(summaries)
    if frontier_rows:
        table(frontier_rows)
        fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2,3.8))
        for rate,color in ((1e-3,"#477da8"),(1e-4,"#c18544")):
            rows=sorted((r for r in frontier_rows if r["p"]==rate),key=lambda r:r["physical qubits"])
            if rows:
                ax.plot([r["physical qubits"] for r in rows],[r["calculated population runtime (s)"] for r in rows],"o-",color=color,label=f"p={rate:g}")
        ax.set_xlabel("Conditional peak physical qubits")
        ax.set_ylabel("Calculated full-population runtime (s)")
        ax.set_title("Port candidate in the unchanged surface-code model")
        ax.legend(frameon=False); ax.spines[["top","right"]].set_visible(False)
        fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
        print("These saved points are conditional model outcomes. The repeated trial population and hardware schedule are unexecuted.")
    else:
        print("No feasible physical point was returned in these saved bounded outcomes. Physical qubits and runtime remain unavailable.")

All six Pareto points, both full feasible sets and every failure component are retained in results.json. Required magic states remain 10,119,826,704, minimal full-pipeline retry cap 7, and separate readiness bound 0.00010119826704. Offline word reconstruction, coefficient/circuit/synthesis preprocessing and final statistical reporting wall time are excluded from quantum runtime. Interface certification, measured decoder throughput and hardware calibration remain unavailable.

These are model-feasible points for one matched task. The original schedule has no evaluated qubit, runtime or spacetime denominator, so no relative savings ratio is reported. The large serialized runtimes are retained; the reports do not establish measured hardware advantage or full-family physical confidence.

Reproduction and evidence limits¶

The saved companion notebook checks retained word matrices, correlated densities/laws and accounting. It has eight executed code cells and three saved figures, with repository and standalone-download replays recorded. It imports no implementation source and repeats no full candidate density run, synthesis or Native query. The separate immutable release gate requires both complete profile statuses, all 33 bundle files, source/recipe identities, complete feasible sets, counters and budgets before site publication.

The 157 Native Trace digests are audit-trusted. Raw Native Trace JSON and the inline audit script/hash were not saved. Saved-record integrity and accounting checks therefore do not claim independent raw Trace replay. The two retained profile-object serialization digests are checked separately under the frozen writer format; this does not verify a private checkpoint’s contents or reconstruct a Native Trace. No Lean formalization is integrated.

Candidate build/check/export and controller eligibility took 310.19 s; the two Native children took 14.75/13.24 s. The recorded whole-worker peak was 1,526,071,296 bytes, below its 2 GiB cap. The candidate-boundary 365,543,424-byte value was measured before artifact serialization and is not the whole-worker peak. These are classical job measurements, separate from the modeled quantum space and time.

  • Complete bundle README, manifest, inventory, fixed recipe, source proof

  • Phase-aware word catalogue, example word QASM, complete candidate QASM

  • Bounded repository runner, word recovery, initialized-path rewrite, conditional resource adapter
